purpose: A source-attributed public-document corpus for a small Demo 1 retrieval pilot about concrete-related RFI information preparation for the Seattle Aquarium Ocean Pavilion.
scope_notice: These records summarize public project updates, case studies, engineering descriptions, owner materials, and public meeting comments. They are not approved construction specifications, submittals, inspection acceptance criteria, or actual RFI records.

records.title: Important Milestone Reached on Seattle Aquarium Ocean Pavilion
records.location_note: Article body, concrete tank pour and formwork description
records.limits: Project update, not an issued-for-construction drawing or contract specification. Preserve Turner's wording and units when answering.

chunks.text: Turner Construction reports that the Ocean Pavilion main tank wall is at least 2 feet thick and that the tank pour used 680 cubic yards of concrete and 355 tons of reinforcing steel. Turner describes the reinforcement amount as about four times that of a typical core.

Turner reports that the non-straight tank geometry required 229 foam formwork panels. The panels were CNC cut, attached to PERI backing, and coated with truck-bed liner. Rhino and Grasshopper were used to work with the tank's double-curved concrete geometry.

records.title: Concrete, steel testing helps bring Seattle Aquarium to life
records.limits: Terracon reports project facts and testing work; the article is not the approved mix design or contract specification. It calls the 10,000 psi material grout, not concrete.

chunks.topic: reported tank material and placement challenge
chunks.text: Terracon describes a custom-built 325,000-gallon tank. It reports nearly 3 million pounds of reinforcing steel in the walls and says standard concrete was unsuitable because aggregate could separate before settling in the congested reinforcement. A high-strength 10,000 psi grout was chosen instead.

Terracon reports that inspectors examined reinforcement and grout in sections as the tank was built, completed nearly 650 material tests, and performed field and laboratory testing that included concrete, shotcrete, and grout.

records.title: Seattle Aquarium Ocean Pavilion
records.limits: Attribute product-performance and project-use statements to Hycrete. The case study does not provide an approved project dosage, mix design, or acceptance criterion.

chunks.text: Hycrete's case study says Hycrete Endure WP, formerly Hycrete W1000, was used as a concrete additive for the saltwater tank. Hycrete describes the product as waterproofing the concrete and forming a protective layer over reinforcing steel to help protect against corrosion.
Hycrete's case study describes the curved saltwater tank as having a capacity of 360,000 gallons.

records.title: Seattle Aquarium Ocean Pavilion
records.limits: Provides structural context, not design calculations, approved dimensions, or material acceptance requirements.

chunks.topic: tank structural role and design context
chunks.text: MKA describes the geometrically complex, cantilevered concrete tank as part of the building's primary gravity- and lateral-force-resisting systems. The page says the tank's unusual geometry and sloshing water effects affected seismic design and detailing.
MKA says the tank design incorporated 3D printing and computer numerical control for custom-cut formwork.

records.title: Ocean Pavilion Progress
records.limits: High-level milestone descriptions; not a detailed schedule, trade sequence, or technical specification.

chunks.text: Seattle Aquarium groups construction into four phases: site preparation, including excavation and deep soil mixing; foundation and lower-level construction; creating the building form, including shell, core, roof, and habitat formwork; and completing interiors, habitats, exhibits, and the rooftop public space.

records.title: Seattle Aquarium 2022 Annual Report
records.location_note: Page 10, 'The Ocean Pavilion rises into the sky'
records.limits: A construction progress quantity, not an approved concrete quantity or performance requirement.

chunks.text: Seattle Aquarium's 2022 annual report says 1,700 cubic feet of concrete was poured for the Ocean Pavilion foundation during the construction progress described in the report.

chunks.text: The Design Commission minutes say commissioners appreciated the project's use of sustainable materials, specifically low-carbon concrete and cement.
